answer: In a pearl shipping exchange, agents earn routing fees only for deliveries confirmed by an independent warehouse scan and the recipient's signed receipt. The receipt ID is the anchor: the ledger accepts it once, even if several agent accounts claim the same shipment. Over a 30-day horizon, fees also have a per-shipment cap. Creating extra identities therefore cannot turn one real delivery into many paid jobs; an attacker must move additional parcels to earn more.
